headlines.title: Teen lifeguard who saved boy at beach in Santa Cruz to meet with President Trump
headlines.description: The teenage lifeguard who saved a young swimmer at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz in July will meet with President Donald Trump at the White House on Monday. Ryder Williams, the 16-year-old lifeguard who rushed into the water to save a 10-year-old child who was overwhelmed by wave after wave last month, will meet President Donald Trump on Monday afternoon at the Oval Office, according to the official White House schedule. The rescue was caught on a video that was watched by millions, including Trump. Trump called the young man “heroic” and said he had plans to invite him and his family to the White House to receive a high civilian honor. “We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor,” Trump said in a post on social media. “Very brave, he deserves it!” Santa Cruz Aug 4 Santa Cruz Aug 2 Santa Cruz Jul 30 Williams said he received help from Aaron Bohnen, another lifeguard, and both brought the kid back to the shore. “This is my job and I love what I do,” Williams wrote in a statement. “I’m thankful to my fellow lifeguards who perform rescues just like this every day.”

headlines.title: San Franciscans brace for heavier traffic during Broadway tunnel construction
headlines.description: A major traffic artery in San Francisco was closed Sunday and will remain partially closed starting on Monday and continuing through the next 14 months. The Robert C. Levy Tunnel, commonly known as the Broadway Tunnel near Russian Hill, Nob Hill, Chinatown and North Beach, is undergoing a major rennovation. It was closed starting at 7 a.m. Sunday and is slated to partially reopen by 5 a.m. on Monday, just as San Francisco Unified students are returning for their first day back to school San Francisco Public Works explained that the tunnel has two bores, and for the first seven months the eastbound bore will be closed, and for the following seven months, the westbound bore will be closed. In the meantime whichever bore is open will carry two-way traffic, a Public Works spokesperson said. The city said this work is for the Chinatown Public Health Center rennovation project, which is paid for through bond money voters approved in 2024. The center is located on top of the tunnel, and the city said the closures are necessary in order to complete this work. The Chinatown Public Health Center “is the most seismically vulnerable public health clinic” in San Francisco, according to the city, and these changes are designed to improve both the center and the tunnel. “We know it’s going to be an inconvenience for drivers, we’re going to try to make it as painless as we can for them, but we will ask drivers to expect delays if they’re going to be using the Broadway tunnel,” said Rachel Gordon with San Francisco Public Works. The city suggests that drivers who want to avoid delays during peak traffic times should take local detours. San Francisco Public Works has been trying to alert local schools and community groups about these changes. However, some neighbors in the area said Sunday they were not aware of this long-term partial closure of the tunnel. “[Broadway is] a main line from Pacific Heights down to Embarcadero you know, even further, so I think it will be a big impact,” said Marissa Marsh of San Francisco. Marsh, who lives near Russian Hill, has kids going back to school on Monday and is bracing for increased traffic on the streets around the tunnel. “I will be avoiding it 100% no doubt,” she said.

headlines.title: ICE says proposed detention facility near Gilroy might hold up to 10 detainees at a time
headlines.description: In a new court filing, ICE rejected the state and county’s estimate that as many as 150 people could be detained in the proposed ICE detainment facility near Gilroy. Instead, the agency says about 10 detainees total might be held at one time, but it added that maximum occupancy would be determined once remodeling is complete. The new documents provide the clearest information yet about ICE’s plan to turn an area near Gilroy into a holding facility. The state of California and Santa Clara County are suing the federal government to stop the project.

headlines.title: Broadway tunnel in San Francisco to close from Sunday to Monday
headlines.description: The Broadway tunnel in San Francisco will be closed Sunday morning into Monday morning, followed by partial lane closures for the next 14 months. The full closure is coming from Sunday at 7 a.m. to Monday at 5 a.m. “This is to accommodate the renovation, the rebuilding of the Chinatown Public Health Center, this is one of the most used public health centers in San Francisco’s Public Health System and the health center sits right on top of the Broadway tunnel, so this is a major seismic undertaking that were doing with a lot of construction there,” Rachel Gordon, with the SF Public Works, said. The 22-hour closure will then be followed by partial lane closures, lasting at least a year. “Starting Monday, we’re going to have partial lane closures for the next 14 months for the Broadway tunnel, so the Broadway tunnel has two bores, one going east bound, one going west bound, we will only have one bore open at a time for the next 14 months,” Gordon said. Drivers say they will be looking for alternate routes. “I just heard a little bit about how it was going to affect my commute and that, because of that, my drive was going to become, it would take longer, because everybody would be taking different routes”, Marina said. San Francisco Public Works say the eastbound bore going into the Chinatown area will be closed first. They will be running two-way traffic and then the westbound bore is going to be closed for the next seven months after that, and there will be two-way traffic with reduced lanes. The lane closures come during a busy time for traffic with schools starting on Monday.

headlines.title: Thousands attend Oakland 16th annual Pride Parade and Festival
headlines.description: Thousands of people came out in downtown Oakland Sunday for the 16th annual Pride Parade and Festival. The theme this year was celebrating “Pride, Power, and People.” People lined up the street to watch and cheer. Music filled the street, while people waved flags as community groups, organizations, and floats made their way along the parade route. “Supporting Oakland Pride and my cousin is visiting from Virginia and I thought it would be fun to show her a local kind of thing and I’m queer,” Berkeley resident Dru said. A sense of LGBTQ community and diversity rooted in Oakland. “It really is, I think a really is a beautiful slice of what life out here is about especially right now, given these political times we are living in,” San Leandro Dawn Surratt said. About 30,000 people were expected at the Parade and Festival. “Oakland is activated for Pride, and we are so excited because this is a new chapter in the life of Pride. Earlier this year, in January, the Oakland LGBTQ Center became the new operators of Oakland Pride,” CEO Co-Founder Oakland LGBTQ Center & Oakland Pride Joe Hawkins said.

headlines.title: Good Samaritan shot intervening in attempted robbery at Alameda shopping center
headlines.description: A good Samaritan was shot in the leg while intervening in an attempted robbery in a South Shore Center parking lot in Alameda, authorities said. Alameda Police Department officers responded to the shopping center at approximately 1:15 p.m. on Saturday, following a report of gunfire. During the preliminary investigation, officers learned that an individual approached a victim and demanded their property. When the victim refused, a struggle ensued. A good Samaritan who witnessed the incident attempted to intervene and assist the victim, police said. During the struggle, a firearm was produced and discharged once, striking the good Samaritan in the leg. The first victim was treated and released at the scene. The good Samaritan was transported to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. The suspect was arrested at the scene and subsequently transported to a local hospital. While an arrest has been made, police noted the investigation into the circumstances and events leading up to the incident remains active and ongoing. “We take incidents like this extremely seriously. Acts of violence are unwelcome in the City of Alameda,” Alameda Police Chief Nishant Joshi said in a statement. “Our officers and investigators will continue working diligently to determine the circumstances surrounding this incident. We have full confidence in the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office to prosecute incidents like these and hold those responsible accountable.”

headlines.title: San Francisco lowers speed limits, increases traffic enforcement around schools
headlines.description: San Francisco is lowering speed limits around schools, increasing traffic enforcement, and continuing to provide crossing guards as students return to class Monday, Mayor Daniel Lurie’s administration announced Friday. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency is expanding 15- and 20-mph speed limits near schools under a state law and plans to phase out 25-mph school-zone limits at more than 230 public and private schools by 2028, a press release noted. The state requires California cities to make the changes by 2031. The city also is expanding traffic enforcement around schools. Automated speed cameras, operating at 33 locations since March 2025, have contributed to an almost 80% decline in speeding citywide. At schools with cameras, speeding has fallen by as much as 94% compared with levels before the cameras were installed, the city said. SFMTA also will introduce Muni changes beginning Aug. 29, including a new one-seat ride from Visitacion Valley to Francisco Middle School and a new 28R Rapid stop near 19th Ave. and Eucalyptus Drive to make it more convenient for Lowell High School students, according to the city. Several major routes also will receive increased frequency or capacity.

headlines.title: Person killed when car drove off of cliff in Santa Cruz was a student, authorities say
headlines.description: Authorities said the person killed when a car drove off of a cliff in Santa Cruz on Thursday was a UC Santa Cruz student. investigators say two people were in the car on West Cliff Drive, when, for some reason, the car left the road and fell down the cliff and into the water. One person was able to get out of the car on their own. Rescue swimmers pulled the other person out of the submerged car, but they died at the hospital. Authorities have only identified the person as a UC Santa Cruz student but have not provided a name or age.

headlines.title: Firefighters halt progress of brush fire in the East Bay
headlines.description: Firefighters were battling a brush fire in the East Bay on Saturday, according to Cal Fire. Cal Fire said the forward progress of the blaze, dubbed the Grant Fire, was stopped as it burned up to 7 acres. The fire was reported in the area of I-580 near Grant Line Road. headlines.title: Proposed innovation center in downtown Oakland triggers questions, concerns
headlines.description: A proposed project in the heart of downtown Oakland, referred to by some as a data center, is raising concerns about its environmental impact and actual economic benefits, but the developer insists it is not a data center. Behring Companies said it’s planning to convert some 20,000 square feet of a building on 20th Street into what it calls an innovation campus. “Data center is typically a bunch of racks and computers for outside parties,” Colin Behring said. “It’s dark. There’s no people in it. That’s not what we can do here.” Behring said the facility could provide computing power for AI, robotics and other tech startups as part of a larger innovation campus surrounding the 19th Street BART station. The building has a history of housing computers. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory once operated a federal supercomputing facility at the site, which Behring said makes it easier to convert the building to house shelves of memory-rich computers now. Many call that a data center, and they have questions about the environmental footprint along with water and power usage. Behring said that wouldn’t be a problem with their center. “California produces so much power that we actually throw away like 3.5 million megawatts of solar and other clean energy every single year because we can’t even store it,” Behring said. District 3 Councilmember Carroll Fife organized a community meeting Friday to let people question the developer directly. Fife said she wants to make sure there are benefits to the average Oakland resident. “We know of all of the concerns that have happened across the country with these large-scale mega facilities coming into low-income communities, people of color communities that don’t have the resources to push back,” she said. Fife said the Oakland Planning and Building Department received Behring’s proposal a week ago for an AI campus. “I want it to be absolutely, critically clear that this is not the large-scale mega facility that people have expressed,” Fife said.

headlines.title: Terra restaurant inside San Jose's Eataly closes due to vermin contamination, officials say
headlines.description: The Terra restaurant on the third floor of Eataly closed due to vermin contamination, according to the County of Santa Clara Environmental Health on Friday. Authorities said an inspection was conducted in the entire Eataly food facility after the department received a public complaint denouncing the presence of rodents. They said that, although the investigation did not find rodents, it confirmed the presence of vermin on the third floor. According to the Department of Environmental Health Official Inspection Report, the inspector “found a live cockroach crawling on the wall above the hand wash sink in the kitchen.” The report also stated they found “dead cockroaches in the following areas: on the wall above the hand wash sink in the food preparation area.” The health permit for Terra Restaurant and Bar was then suspended, according to health authorities. They said the restaurant manager confirmed during an interview with Environmental Health inspectors that pest control services were completed Thursday night, the facility was thoroughly cleaned and sanitized and food that was potentially contaminated was thrown away. Officials said the restaurant will reopen as soon as it resolves all open items from the inspection report and requests a reinspection to confirm the problem was resolved. NBC Bay Area reached out to Eataly for comment but hasn’t heard back.

headlines.title: Hayward Fire Department opens applications for free fall chipping program
headlines.description: The Hayward Fire Department is accepting applications for its Fall Chipping program, offering free vegetation chipping to eligible residents as part of an effort to reduce wildfire risk in high-hazard areas. Applications will be accepted through Oct. 1, with chipping scheduled between Sept. 1 and Nov. 13, or until program funding runs out. Services are available on a first-come, first-served basis, and officials are encouraging residents to apply early. Residents must cut, gather, and stack branches at the front of their property. A city-contracted crew will chip the material at the curb on a scheduled service day. The program is part of Hayward Fire’s Wildfire Ready East Bay initiative, which aims to help residents create defensible space around homes by removing dry vegetation and tree limbs. Residents can apply through the 2026 Chipping Program at www.hayward-ca.gov/ChipperProgram. Applicants can select a preferred chipping session after submitting a request and will receive an email confirming participation.
